items.caption:
Have you ever had a moment where your heart told you, “this isn’t the right choice,” even when everything on paper seemed as if it were the “right choice” or “right path” to take?

The more you sharpen your sensitivity to Tokimeki, the more clearly you begin to hear your heart and intuition💛

When you practice noticing what truly sparks joy, your decisions become less about what you should choose and more about what genuinely makes you feel alive.

Over time, you may find yourself choosing work, relationships, opportunities, and experiences that align with your heart rather than external expectations.

Tokimeki isn’t just about what you keep in your home. It’s a way of reconnecting with yourself and learning to trust your inner voice and taking action towards what makes you alive.

Join us at @artoftokimeki and check out their bio to join our community!

#artoftokimeki #tokimeki #sparkjoy #career #journaling
items.transcript: The more you practice Tokimeki, following your inner spark of joy, the clearer your career decisions become. You might pass on an opportunity that looks perfect on paper because deep down you know it's not right for you. Or you might say yes to a path that makes no logical sense, simply because it's right you are. When sharpening your sensitivity for Tokimeki, your career begins to unfold in ways you never could have imagined. That's its power. You choose the path of joy. Tokimeki doesn't just change your work, it will change your entire life.

items.caption:
Welcome back to the Weekly Tokimeki Question! Today, we’re looking a little closer at our workspaces: What’s one item on your desk that sparks Tokimeki for you?✨

For Marie, it’s her trusted mechanical pencil, a series she’s been loyal to for over ten years. She loves its compact size, the perfect fit in her hand, the smooth grip, and the effortless way it writes. It’s a simple tool, but everything about it brings a sense of comfort and joy to her everyday work.

It doesn't have to be fancy or extraordinary. So many of the objects supporting our daily flow often go unnoticed, yet they hold a quiet power to make work feel a little lighter and more grounded.

Take a moment right now to look at your desk. Pick up or look at that one item, and stay with the feeling for just a few seconds. Notice how it feels in your body. This is how we begin to cultivate our sensitivity to Tokimeki, by slowing down, noticing joy in the functional, and allowing ourselves to appreciate the everyday things that support us.

📌 Share yours with us below, in a photo or a comment! What’s the desk item that supports you? We'll be featuring some of your answers in an upcoming post💛

#artoftokimeki #reflection #journalprompt #journaling #workspace

Welcome back to the Weekly Tokimeki Question! Today we’re keeping it simple: what is one small thing that made you smile today? ✨

For Marie, it was recently, while she was taking a walk with her son, when he got interested in a fallen leaf and picked it up, and it was so cute. His lively, happy expression made her smile.

It doesn’t have to be big. Sometimes life’s greatest joys can be found in the smallest moments, the ones we tend to rush past.

Think of that small thing and stay with the feeling for just a few seconds. Notice how it feels in your body. This is how we begin to cultivate our sensitivity to Tokimeki, by slowing down, noticing joy, and allowing ourselves to fully experience it.

📌 Share yours with us below, in a photo or a comment! We’ll be featuring some of your answers in an upcoming post💛

#artoftokimeki #reflection #journalprompt #journaling #sparkjoy
items.transcript: Let's try something simple today. Think of one small thing that made you smile today. Just one. It doesn't have to be big. A kind word, a quiet moment, a cup of tea. Stay with that feeling for a few seconds. If you'd like, share it. What is one small thing that made you smile today?
